name: Scelidosaurus V2
description: Scelidosaurus was an early herbivorous dinosaur that lived during the Early Jurassic period, around 200 to 190 million years ago. Measuring about 4.5 meters (15 feet) in length, it was one of the earliest known armored dinosaurs, featuring rows of bony plates and spikes along its back and tail for defense. Scelidosaurus had a low, broad body with a relatively small head and a beak-like mouth, adapted for consuming low-lying vegetation. Its fossils have been found in what is now the United Kingdom, providing important insights into the evolution of ankylosaurs and their adaptations.

name: foreign body (wire) horse
description:
a foreign body (wire) in the intestines of a horse 

size of specimen: 143.5 x 72.5 x 36.4 mm

Scanning performed with the structured light scanners "Artec Leo" and "Artec Spider"

Pathogenesis: Ingested wire penetrates the intestinal wall and may migrate into the peritoneal cavity or adjacent organs, causing local and septic peritonitis and abscess formation.

Etiology: Metallic wires originating from bedding, forage, fencing or stable hardware.

Epidemiology: Uncommon; reported in multiple case series with substantial morbidity and guarded prognosis if diagnosis/treatment delayed.

Clinical signs: Acute or chronic colic, abdominal pain, fever, anorexia, weight loss, tachycardia, reduced gut sounds.

Diagnostics: Radiography (radiopaque wire), abdominal ultrasound, abdominocentesis with fluid analysis, exploratory laparotomy/necropsy

description:
This is a 3D mesh  of an approximately 1-year old  leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea). 

This 3D model was created in collaboration with Upwell Turtles (www.upwell.org) and their partners at the Thailand Department of Marine and Coastal Resources and Phuket Marine Biological Center, who provided photos of leatherbacks at this rarely observed life stage. 

Existing data on leatherbacks was also referenced. CG artist Johnson Martin used these data to reconstruct and animate the model using Blender software. Upwell provided the funding for this research.

Special thanks to Dr. George Shillinger, Dr. Kristin Reed, Elle Onsathit and Kayla Sargent of Upwell; Dr. Pinsak Suraswadi and Hirun Kanghae of the Phuket Marine Biological Center.

Downloads are freely available for creative and non-profit use.  To inquire about licensing, please visit www.digitallife3d.org

name: Costas Argyrou Museum - Owl or Thoupos 1980
description: Owls or thoupia were featured in his solo exhibitions in 1980, 1984, and 1992. The works Thoupos (88) and Owl I, mother of Owl II and III (89), made of porous stone from Skarinou, are the oldest and bear deeper engravings than the later works on the same theme. The work Owl I was included among the pieces with which he participated in the 1981 International Exhibition of Small Sculpture in Budapest, where he (Costas Argyrou) received one of the honorary diplomas. Later, in 1985, he created two more owls (90 and 91) from limestone, clarifying that they are the children of the first. Around the same time, he also created the work Owl IV (92). The work Koukouvaouthkia I (93), presented in his 1984 solo exhibition, and Koukouvaouthkia II (94), depict — the former — a group of three, and — the latter — a group of two small owls.

name: Sloth
description:
The sloth is a slow-moving mammal native to the tropical forests of Central and South America. Sloths are known for their long limbs, curved claws, and slow, deliberate movements, which help them conserve energy.
They spend most of their lives hanging upside down in trees, feeding on leaves, fruits, and flowers. Their slow metabolism and specialized diet allow them to survive on relatively little food.
Sloths are also excellent swimmers and have a unique relationship with algae that grow on their fur, which provides camouflage in the forest canopy.
Overall, sloths are fascinating creatures, perfectly adapted to life in the trees, and play an important role in the health of tropical forest ecosystems.

This 3D model was realized by Clarissa Bignoli and Erika Del Bene during the Universal Civil Service (SCU) at UniGe.

name: Fire-Frilled Three-Horned Face - dinosaur
description:
**Triceratops ignifrons: A Landmark Ceratopsid Discovery in Alberta**

In 2022, paleontologist Dr. Miriam Solano uncovered a striking ceratopsid specimen in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, Canada. Named *Triceratops ignifrons*—“Fire-Frilled Three-Horned Face”—this quadrupedal herbivore measured over 9 meters in length and featured an unusually elaborate frill with spiked margins and preserved pigment structures.

Spectroscopic analysis revealed traces of structural coloration, suggesting vivid blue, orange, and red hues across its frill and flanks. This challenges prior assumptions that ceratopsids relied solely on size and horn morphology for display. The discovery of *T. ignifrons* provides compelling evidence for visual signaling in herbivorous dinosaurs and deepens our understanding of social behavior and predator deterrence in Late Cretaceous ecosystems.

Chaque courbe et chaque pli du corps du raptor sont finement sculptés, offrant une topologie propre et optimisée pour une intégration fluide dans vos projets. Idéal pour le rendu photoréaliste ou même l'impression 3D, ce modèle est un atout précieux pour tout fan de Jurassic Park. Sa pose naturelle et expressive apporte une touche d'innocence et de réalisme à vos décors.

Ajoutez ce chef-d'œuvre de sculpture numérique à votre collection et donnez vie à vos créations avec un réalisme saisissant.

name: Nest - Superb fairy-wren
description:
**superb fairy-wren,* Malurus cyaneus***

The female fairy-wren alone builds a dome-shaped nest with a side entrance, made of grasses, bark fibre and some spider webs. Nests are lined with feathers and sometimes with fur or thistle down. The nest is usually built less than one metre to the ground, often well concealed amongst thick vegetation such as blackberry bushes, ferns or dense grass.

The superb fairy wren lays three to four white eggs speckled with pale reddish-brown  markings.

QVM:1981:2:0005

Learn more about the [male superb fairy-wren ♂ ](https://sketchfab.com/models/9ec0bb0e43e24ec1a9a8d37ec21d7a91/embed),  the [female superb fairy-wren ♀ ](https://sketchfab.com/models/5aa43c47cc65497c8fe60ec769a20e57/embed)

description:
There are a huge number of snakes in the world, and each of them is unique in its own way.

Taipans are a genus of highly venomous snakes of the elapidae family.
These are large Australian snakes whose bite is considered the most dangerous among modern snakes.

The taipan lives on the coast of northern and north-eastern Australia and in the south-east of New Guinea. It leads a predominantly diurnal lifestyle. It feeds on frogs and small mammals, including mice and rats.

______________________________

В мире существует огромное количество змей, и каждая из них по-своему уникальна.

Тайпаны — род очень ядовитых змей семейства аспидов.
Это крупные австралийские змеи, укус которых считается самым опасным среди современных змей.

Тайпан обитает на побережье северной и северо-восточной Австралии и на юго-востоке Новой Гвинеи. Ведет преимущественно дневной образ жизни. Питается лягушками и мелкими млекопитающими, в том числе мышами и крысами.

name: Hippopotamus
description:
3D scan of the skull of an adult Hippopotamus (*Hippopotamus amphibius*). 

The hippopotamus is a large semiaquatic mammal native to sub-Saharan Africa. Adults average weight is 1,500 kg and are 2.90 to 5.05 m long. Despite its stocky shape and short legs, it is capable of running 30 km/h over short distances.  It inhabits rivers, lakes, and mangrove swamps where spends most the day in water to stay cool and hydrated. Just before night begins, they leave the water to forage on land. Its diet consists almost entirely of grass, with only minimal consumption of aquatic plants.



Specimen: Hippopotamus, *Hippopotamus amphibius* Linnaeus, 1758

Inventory number: C 228

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

The whimsical edit was so amusing that the fish was forever after known as Spoon, a name that stuck as a reminder of the quirky creativity behind its transformation. 

In short, Spoon is an inside joke

name: Tick
description:
**Tick (Ixodida order)**
   - Parasitic arachnids that feed on blood.
   - Known for spreading diseases like Lyme disease.

Ticks (order Ixodida) are parasitic arachnids that feed on the blood of mammals, birds, and reptiles. Though tiny, they pose serious health risks due to their ability to transmit diseases like Lyme disease, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, and anaplasmosis. Ticks latch onto hosts using specialized mouthparts, piercing the skin and feeding for hours or even days.

Found in grassy, wooded, and humid environments, ticks are most active during warmer months. They detect hosts through body heat and carbon dioxide, then climb aboard to feed. After engorging, they drop off to continue their life cycle.

Preventing tick bites involves wearing protective clothing, using repellents, and checking for ticks after outdoor activities. Despite their reputation, ticks play a role in ecosystems, but their potential to spread disease makes awareness and prevention essential.

name: Water deer
description:
3D scan of the mandible of a water deer (*Hydropotes inermis*).

The water deer is a small deer species native to Korea and China characterized by prominent tusks, similar to those of musk deer. It inhabits the land alongside rivers, where they are protected from sight by the tall reeds and rushes. It is a proficient swimmer, and can swim several miles to reach remote river islands. It has a body length of 77-100 cm with a tail of 6-7,5 cm.


Specimen: Water deer, *Hydropotes inermis* Swinhoe, 1870

Inventory number: C 1292

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Simone Farina

name: Amethystine Blight Queen
description:
At the heart of every *Beetle Rubigenum* Colony is the Queen. Almost spider-like in appearance, the Queen's sole purpose is to manage the hive and birth new workers and/or soldiers. 

The *Amethystine Blight Queen* is the most exotic variant, living within it's hive deep inside Amethyst-rich cave systems. It is also the weakest variant, having gained no mutations other than it's pigmentation, designed to blend in with it's environment. It's shell is fragile compared to it's cousin variants, but it more than makes up for it's own weaknesses with it's agility and use of deception. Due to it's lightweight shell, it is able to leap a considerable distance despite it's size. 

**Other Things to Note:** *Some have reported entire clusters of amethyst growing on the shells of these Queens. It is hypothesized that these Queens use this as a lure.*

This asset contains 11 animations including Idle, Combat, and Walk animations.

Modeled, retopologized, rigged and animated in Blender. Textured in Quixel Mixer.

name: Glyptonotus antarcticus
description:
Glyptonotus antarcticus Eights, 1852 is a benthic marine isopod crustacean in the suborder Valvifera. This relatively large isopod is found in the Southern Ocean around Antarctica. This 3D model is from a specimen (MNA-02712) collected in the framework of the National Science Foundation (NSF) ICEFISH 2004 cruise.

G. antarcticus is a powerful carnivore and scavenger, an ecological role that brings this species to be caught in baited traps. It capable of active swimming, which is performed in an upside-down position.

Eggs and young are brooded for more than one year in the female’s marsupium formed by a series of specisalized appendages (oostegites). Here the eggs are nourished by a maternal secretion.

Respiratory chamber is located ventrally to the pleotelson, consisting in two leaf-like uropods, that ventilate the animal; also pleopods, thin and flattened, help the respiratory processes with continuous movements.

name: Griffon vulture
description:
3D scan of the heart of griffon vulture (*Gyps fulvus*). 


The griffon vulture is a large Old World vulture in the bird of prey family Accipitridae. It is 93–122 cm long with a 2.3–2.8 m wingspan and a weight of 6.2-10.5 kg. Like other vultures, it is a scavenger, feeding mostly from carcasses of dead animals which it finds by soaring over open areas, often moving in flocks. It grunts and hisses at roosts or when feeding on carrion.


Specimen: Griffon vulture, *Gyps fulvus* (Hablizl, 1783)

Inventory number: AV 7184

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Simone Farina

name: GOLDEN_RETRIEVER
description:
Golden Retriever Bust – 3D Printable Sculptural Model

A clean, realistic 3D bust of a Golden Retriever — designed for 3D printing, hand-painting, and display.
This sculptural model captures the calm and loyal nature of one of the world’s most beloved dog breeds.
Created in the signature Memoteh style, the model features smooth stylized fur, balanced proportions, and a solid cylindrical base for easy printing and stability.

Perfect for:
• Pet lovers and collectors
• 3D printing enthusiasts
• Artists looking for high-quality printable sculptures

Recommended settings:
• Minimum height: 8 cm
• Infill: 10 %
• Tree supports: required
• Material: PLA or matte filament
• Speed: Outer 100 mm/s, Inner 150 mm/s

If you notice ear or surface distortion, lower speeds to 70–80 mm/s and 110–120 mm/s.
Print, paint, and enjoy your own handcrafted Golden Retriever sculpture!

name: Collared peccary
description:
3D scan of the skull of a collared peccary (*Pecari tajacu*). 

The collared peccary is a species in the family Tayassuidae found in North, Central, and South America. It is widespread throughout much of the tropical and subtropical Americas, where inhabits deserts, xeric shrublands, tropical and subtropical grasslands, savannas, shrublands, flooded grasslands and savannas, tropical and subtropical dry broadleaf forests, and several other habitats. It stands around 51–61 cm tall at the shoulder and is about 1.0–1.5 m long. It has an herbivorous diet and it feeds on cactus, mesquite beans, fruits, berries, seeds, roots, tubers, bulbs, even if it also feeds on small vertebrates.


Specimen: Collared peccari, *Pecari tajacu* (Linnaeus, 1758)

Inventory number: C 2709

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa

name: mammoth molar
description: A molar of a woolly mammoth found in the North Sea by a fisherman. Woolly mammoths had four functional molar teeth at a time—two in the upper jaw and two in the lower. About 23 cm (9.1 in) of the crown was within the jaw, and 2.5 cm (0.98 in) was above. The crown was continually pushed forwards and up as it wore down, comparable to a conveyor belt. The teeth had up to 26 separated ridges of enamel, which were themselves covered in “prisms” that were directed towards the chewing surface. These were quite wear-resistant and kept together by cementum and dentine. A mammoth had six sets of molars throughout a lifetime, which were replaced five times. The latter condition could extend the lifespan of the individual, unless the tooth consisted of only a few plates. The first molars were about the size of those of a human, 1.3 cm (0.51 in), the third were 15 cm (5.9 in) long, and the sixth were about 30 cm (12 in) long and weighed 1.8 kg. The molars grew larger and contained more ridges with each replacement.

name: Fossili brown bear (right femur)
description:
3D scan of the right of a  fossil brown bear (*Ursus arctos*). 


Fossil of a prime adult female skull of brown bear. The specimen was found in "Abisso Oriano Coltelli" cave (44°05'35,0 N, 10°14'47,0" E, labelled T/Lu 642 in the Tuscan register of caves) which opens at 1209 m a.s.l on the western slope of "Monte Alto di Sella" (Apuan Alps). The mammal assemblage collected consists of 486 investigated specimens, 127 of which belong to an individual skeleton of brown bear. The bear died from non-violent causes, probably during hibernation. The specimen was dated providing a conventional age of 6480 ± 40 14 C ka BP (Holocene).
More information : https://amq.aiqua.it/index.php/amq/article/view/112



Specimen: Brown bear, *Ursus arctos* Linnaeus, 1758

name: Iberian ribbed newt
description:
Унікальний захист: Іберійський ребристий тритон має незвичайний механізм захисту — коли він відчуває загрозу, то може виштовхувати свої гострі ребра через шкіру на боках тіла, одночасно виділяючи токсичну речовину. Це робить його неприємним для хижаків.
Місце проживання: Цей вид поширений переважно на Піренейському півострові (Іспанія та Португалія) та в деяких частинах північного Марокко. Він віддає перевагу водоймам, таким як ставки, озера чи повільні річки.
Регенерація: Як і багато інших амфібій, іберійський ребристий тритон має вражаючу здатність до регенерації. Він може відновлювати втрачені кінцівки, частини хвоста і навіть деякі внутрішні органи.
Розмір: Це один із найбільших видів тритонів — дорослі особини можуть досягати до 30 см у довжину, включаючи хвіст, що робить його значно більшим за більшість інших тритонів.
Спосіб життя: Ці тритони переважно водні, хоча в певні періоди можуть виходити на сушу.

description:

O modelo apresenta a identificação de alguns elementos ósseos, permitindo a observação de características morfológicas típicas da família Felidae, como crânio robusto e dentição adaptada à predação. 

A onça é o maior felino das Américas e desempenha papel fundamental como predador de topo, regulando populações de presas e contribuindo para a manutenção do equilíbrio ecológico. Trata-se de um dos principais representantes da fauna do Cerrado, um dos biomas mais biodiversos do Brasil.

description:

Unlike many frogs that lay all their eggs together, this species shows very “caring” behavior: the male carries the tadpoles one by one on his back to small pools of water, such as those that form in leaves or plants (phytotelmata).

In Ecuador, it inhabits the tropical humid Amazon rainforest in the provinces of Orellana, Pastaza, and Napo.

It is classified on Ecuador’s Red List of Amphibians under the category Least Concern (Criterion A2d), and on the IUCN Red List of Threatened Species as Least Concern.

name: マガキガイ / Strawberry Conch
description:
和名にある「まがき（籬）」は、竹などで目を粗く編んだ垣根のことで、貝殻表面の模様や色が似ることによる。沖縄の方言では「ティラジャー」といい、貝塚からよく出土する。貝殻からニョキッと飛び出た２本の柄の先には眼がついていて、鎌状のギザギザの蓋で海底を蹴って歩く。眼を見ると食べる気がしないが、茹でると美味しいそうだ。昔は殻頂部分で独楽を作って遊んだようだ。この個体は外唇縁を破損して修復した跡がある。

The Japanese name “magaki” refers to a fence made of bamboo or other materials woven loosely, and is derived from the similarity of the pattern and color of the shell surface. In the Okinawan dialect, it is called “tirajya” and is often excavated from shell mounds. The two handles protruding from the shell have eyes at the tips and use a sickle-shaped, jagged cover to kick the seabed and walk. Looking at the eyes may not make one feel like eating them, but they are said to be delicious when boiled. In the past, people apparently made spinning tops from the shell's apex and played with them. This specimen has traces of repair where the outer lip edge was damaged.

英名：Strawberry Conch

学名：*Strombus (Conomurex) luhuanus* Linnaeus, 1758　
　　　  ソデボラ科　Strombidae

description:

description:
This is a prehistoric horse tooth from the Science Museum of Minnesota Paleontology Colleciton. Catalog Number: SMMFIC.1.4188 (temporary number)

It is unclear if this is a very old modern horse, or if this is a prehistoric extinct horse from the Americas. This tooth is going to be carbon dated. This is a destructive process, so a portion of the tooth will be destroyed. I 3D scanned this tooth so that there will be a record of it’s pre-carbon-dated condition.

This 3D scan is also part of a research grant looking to understand the “best” 3D scanning methodologies. I used photogrammetry to create this image.

name: Gajah Sumatera
description:
Gajah Sumatera adalah subspesies gajah Asia terkecil yang hanya ditemukan di Pulau Sumatera dengan populasi sekitar 2,400-2,800 individu. Mereka memiliki peran vital dalam ekosistem hutan tropis sebagai arsitek hutan yang membantu penyebaran biji-bijian dan membuka jalur di hutan lebat.

Gajah dewasa memiliki tinggi 2-3.2 meter dengan berat mencapai 2,000-4,000 kg. Sebagai herbivora, mereka mengonsumsi daun, rumput, dan buah-buahan dalam jumlah besar setiap harinya. Habitat alami mereka adalah hutan hujan tropis Sumatera, dimana mereka dapat hidup hingga 60-70 tahun di alam liar.

Ancaman utama terhadap keberadaan mereka adalah deforestasi dan konflik dengan manusia akibat penyempitan habitat. Status konservasi mereka saat ini adalah Critically Endangered menurut IUCN, yang menunjukkan urgensi tinggi untuk perlindungan dan pelestarian spesies ini.

name: Fossil brown bear (pelvis and right acetabulum)
description:
3D scan of the pelvis and right acetabulum of a fossil brown bear (*Ursus arctos*). 


Fossil of a prime adult female skull of brown bear. The specimen was found in "Abisso Oriano Coltelli" cave (44°05'35,0 N, 10°14'47,0" E, labelled T/Lu 642 in the Tuscan register of caves) which opens at 1209 m a.s.l on the western slope of "Monte Alto di Sella" (Apuan Alps). The mammal assemblage collected consists of 486 investigated specimens, 127 of which belong to an individual skeleton of brown bear. The bear died from non-violent causes, probably during hibernation. The specimen was dated providing a conventional age of 6480 ± 40 14 C ka BP (Holocene).
More information : https://amq.aiqua.it/index.php/amq/article/view/112


Specimen: Brown bear, *Ursus arctos* Linnaeus, 1758

Inventory number: I17771

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

name: Royal Nghe Statue - Hue Imperial City
description:
Royal Nghe Statue - Hue Imperial City | Tượng Nghê Điện Thái Hòa - Linh vật cung đình Huế

A detailed 3D reconstruction of the Nghe statue at Thai Hoa Palace, located within the Hue Imperial City (UNESCO Heritage). In Vietnamese culture, the Nghe is a mythical creature symbolizing wisdom, loyalty, and majesty, traditionally placed in royal spaces for protection. This model showcases the sophisticated bronze craftsmanship of the Nguyen Dynasty. Ideal for digital museums, architectural studies, and Vietnamese cultural projects.

Mô hình 3D phục dựng chi tiết tượng Nghê tại Điện Thái Hòa, thuộc quần thể di sản cố đô Huế. Trong văn hóa Việt Nam, Nghê là linh vật biểu tượng cho sự thông minh, trung thành và uy nghiêm, thường được đặt tại các không gian cung đình để canh giữ và trừ tà. description:
Zhu Ba Jie - Introduction

# Due to the limit of words, please translate the introduction below.

猪八戒，又名猪刚鬣、猪悟能，是古典名著《西游记》中的人物。

原是天庭玉皇大帝手下的天蓬元帅，主管天河，因醉酒调戏嫦娥，拱倒了斗牛宫，吃了王母灵芝菜，被玉皇大帝逐出天界，到人间投胎，却又错投猪胎，嘴脸与猪相似。下凡后“嫁”给卵二姐，栖身云栈洞，后被观音菩萨指点归于佛门，法号悟能，于高老庄等候取经人时入赘高太公家。唐僧西去取经路过高老庄，被孙悟空收服，拜唐僧为师。唐僧因猪八戒“老实”，平常多袒护猪八戒而责备孙悟空，猪八戒也好进谗言，多次挑唆唐僧与孙悟空的关系，导致唐僧两次将孙悟空赶走，直到“真假美猴王”之后，师徒之间才剪除二心，同心戮力，赶奔西天，遇到妖怪时，猪八戒开始敢于争先，成为孙悟空的好帮手，兄弟合力打败牛魔王、九头虫、豹子精、蟒蛇精等许多妖怪，虽然仍贪图美色，但定力较之前好了许多，打死玉面狐狸、万圣公主、杏仙等多个女妖。取得真经后，如来封猪八戒为“净坛使者”菩萨。

猪八戒身上既有人的吃苦耐劳、憨厚率直的品质以及贪婪自私的本性，又有神的本领，同时还有猪的形体特征，这充分体现了作者把人性、神性、猪性的完美结合。

name: Red-throated loon
description:
3D scan of the heart of red-throated loon (*Gavia stellata*). 

The red-throated loon is a migratory aquatic bird found in the northern hemisphere. It breeds primarily in Arctic regions, and winters in northern coastal waters. During the breeding season, it acquires the distinctive reddish throat patch which is the basis for its common name. It measures from 55 to 67 cm in length, weighing 1-2.7 kg and is the smallest and lightest of the world's loons. It feeds mainly on fish,  but also on amphibians, invertebrates, and plants.



Specimen: Red-throated Loon, *Gavia stellata* (Pontoppidan, 1763)

Inventory number: AV 7184

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

name: osteophytes cat
description:
size of specimen: 45.8 x 80.2 x 57.3 mm

3D scanning performed with the structured light scanner Artec Space Spider 

Etiology: Marked periosteal osteophyte formation of uncertain origin; chronic dietary hypervitaminosis A is suspected, as excess retinol can induce abnormal bone proliferation in cats.

Pathogenesis: Persistent osteoblastic stimulation with reduced resorption causes excessive periosteal bone apposition. Irregular osteophytes form on the skull and nearby joints, limiting mobility and potentially compressing nerves.

Epidemiology: Uncommon; often linked to prolonged liver-rich feeding, though other metabolic or inflammatory factors may contribute.

Clinical Signs: Painful or stiff head/neck movement, reduced jaw opening, reluctance to move, ± neurological deficits with compression.

Diagnosis: Radiography shows extensive periosteal exostoses; CT defines extent. Elevated serum retinol may support suspicion. Histology reveals dense, irregular lamellar bone.

Diplodocus is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic of North America. The first fossils of Diplodocus were discovered in 1877 by S. W. Williston. description:
Print ready dragonfly sculpture.

Measure units are millimeters, the model is about 10 sm in length.


Mesh is manifold, no holes, no inverted faces, no bad contiguous edges.


Available formats: .blend, .stl, .obj, .fbx, .glb

Here are three versions of the model:


1) DF_sld_legs.  Solid(one piece) sculpture with legs, 911150 triangular faces.
2)  DF_sld.  Solid(one piece) sculpture without legs.
3) DF_prts. Separate parts to be printed separately for assembling the whole dragonfly.

Position of the wings can be adjusted after assembling, it can be rotated inside it's sockets.
File Wings_sml.stl contains wings with smaller connection spheres so it can rotate more loosely inside it's sockets.

name: Beaver Skull and Mandible
description:
3D model of the skull and mandible of a one-year-old female beaver (one of 'Pink Tag's' daughters). 

Skeletal preparator Jon Nott prepared the skull and mandible for use in RAMM’s teaching and handling collection with support from Devon Wildlife Trust. The model was produced using Agisoft Metashape and Blender from 760 images.

The surprise arrival of beavers on the River Otter in 2013 caused quite a stir. In 2015, in the midst of public campaigns against their removal, Devon Wildlife Trust began a trial to investigate the effects of a wild-living population of beavers on the river. In August 2020 DEFRA ruled that families of beavers on the River Otter are permitted to remain there. 

For more info visit [RAMM's website](https://rammuseum.org.uk/news/a-very-important-beaver/).

[CC0 - Public Domain](http://creativecommons.org/public-domain/cc0/).

Optional attribution: “Digitisation by the [University of Exeter’s Digital Humanities Lab](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/digitalhumanities/digital-lab/) / RAMM"
